subject.title: [Feature]: Audit log for agent memory changes

question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-class memory mutation audit layer for `MEMORY.md` and `memory/*.md`, and what storage, privacy, tamper-evidence, and event taxonomy should that layer use?
rationale: This cannot be resolved as a narrow code repair because the durable audit store, privacy exposure, tamper-evidence boundary, plugin/API ownership, and cause propagation model are product and security decisions.

options.title: Design core audit layer first
options.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers define the audit event taxonomy, storage/integrity model, privacy rules, and required write-surface coverage before implementation.

options.title: Start with a persistence hook
options.body: Narrow the core work to a generic durable-write hook such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48509, then let memory-core or plugins build audit policy on top.

options.title: Defer to external packages
options.body: Treat Pinchy, world-model-mcp, or a ClawHub package as the supported audit path and close or supersede this core issue only after maintainers decide core memory-file writes do not need first-class auditing.

recommendation.title: Design core audit layer first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers define the audit event taxonomy, storage/integrity model, privacy rules, and required write-surface coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest current routing candidate because the issue discussion already records a design-review keep-open comment and recent commits show adjacent memory flush and memory-doc work.
